svg.data-vd-steps: [[0, "Blood enters the glomerulus through the afferent arteriole. It is wider than the efferent arteriole, so the blood pressure in the glomerulus is high."], [1.6, "Ultrafiltration: water and small molecules (glucose, amino acids, urea, ions) are forced out through the capillary pores, the basement membrane and the podocytes into Bowman\u2019s capsule. Blood cells and large proteins stay in the blood."], [3.3, "Proximal convoluted tubule: selective reabsorption. All the glucose and amino acids, and most of the water and ions, go back into the blood."], [7, "Descending limb of the loop of Henle: permeable to water, so water leaves by osmosis into the salty medulla."], [9.9, "Ascending limb: impermeable to water. Na\u207a and Cl\u207b are pumped out, which keeps the medulla hypertonic (salty)."], [12.3, "Distal convoluted tubule: the ion content and pH of the filtrate are adjusted."], [14, "Collecting duct: water leaves by osmosis through aquaporins into the salty medulla. ADH adds more aquaporins: less urine, more concentrated."], [18, "Urine (water, urea and excess ions, no glucose) flows to the renal pelvis, then the ureter and bladder."]]
svg.title: The nephron and urine formation
svg.desc: A nephron: Bowman’s capsule round the glomerulus, proximal convoluted tubule, loop of Henle, distal convoluted tubule and collecting duct, with the afferent and efferent arterioles and capillaries. Play: ultrafiltration, selective reabsorption, and water and salt movement in the loop and collecting duct.
svg.text: One nephron, simplified and not to scale. Blood vessels are shown only in part.

g.data-info: Outer region of the kidney: glomeruli, Bowman’s capsules and convoluted tubules.
Inner region: loops of Henle and collecting ducts. Its tissue fluid gets saltier (more hypertonic) towards the pelvis.
Capillaries round the tubules and loop: they take back the reabsorbed substances.
Brings blood to the glomerulus. It is wider than the efferent arteriole, which keeps the pressure in the glomerulus high.
Takes blood away from the glomerulus; narrower, so pressure builds up. It leads to the capillaries round the tubules.
Cup-shaped start of the nephron. Its inner wall of podocytes wraps the glomerulus; filtrate collects in the space inside.
A knot of capillaries with pores (fenestrations). High blood pressure forces small molecules out: ultrafiltration.
Selective reabsorption: all glucose and amino acids, and most water and ions, return to the blood. Its cells have microvilli and many mitochondria (active transport).

g.data-name: Descending limb of the loop of Henle
g.data-info: Permeable to water: water leaves by osmosis into the salty medulla.
g.aria-label: Descending limb of the loop of Henle

g.data-info: Hairpin loop that creates a high solute concentration (hypertonic) in the medulla, so water can be reabsorbed from the collecting duct.

g.data-name: Ascending limb of the loop of Henle
g.data-info: Impermeable to water. Na⁺ and Cl⁻ are pumped out (active transport), making the medulla hypertonic.
g.aria-label: Ascending limb of the loop of Henle

g.data-info: Adjusts the ion content of the filtrate (and pH) by selective reabsorption and secretion.
Carries filtrate through the salty medulla: water leaves by osmosis through aquaporins. ADH inserts more aquaporins, so less, more concentrated urine forms.

g.data-name: To the renal pelvis and ureter
g.data-info: Urine (water, urea, excess ions) drains from many collecting ducts into the pelvis, then down the ureter to the bladder.
g.aria-label: To the renal pelvis and ureter

g.data-info: Cortex, medulla (pyramids), pelvis and ureter. About a million nephrons in each kidney.
